$$

question.:question/problem: Given that $a=⟨1,-3,2⟩,$ $b=⟨2,-1,-1⟩,$ and $c=⟨3,-3,0⟩,$ find $a\cdot (b\times c)$ using the definition of the scalar triple product.

$$
\begin{aligned}b\times c & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & -1 & -1 \\ 3 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -3 & 0\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 3 & -3\end{aligned}|k \\  & =((-1)\cdot 0-(-1)\cdot (-3))i-(2\cdot 0-(-1)\cdot 3)j+(2\cdot (-3)-(-1)\cdot 3)k \\  & =-3i-3j-3k \\  & =⟨-3,-3,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can compute the scalar triple product:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =⟨1,-3,2⟩\cdot ⟨-3,-3,-3⟩ \\  & =1\cdot (-3)+(-3)\cdot (-3)+2\cdot (-3) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}b\times c & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -1 & 4\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(3\cdot 4-2\cdot (-1))i-((-1)\cdot 4-2\cdot 2)j+((-1)\cdot (-1)-3\cdot 2)k \\  & =14i+8j-5k \\  & =⟨14,8,-5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can compute the scalar triple product:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =⟨-2,4,3⟩\cdot ⟨14,8,-5⟩ \\  & =(-2)\cdot 14+4\cdot 8+3\cdot (-5) \\  & =-11.\end{aligned}
$$
